q: If allowed, which ceiling finish suits the nursing wards best?
n: An exposed/bare ceiling is easiest to keep clean and free of dust traps, an important consideration for infection control in nursing wards, per the source document.
scenario: Nursing wards are part of the barangay health facility's program.

q: Given its residential surroundings, which amenity should the site plan include?
n: A playground is a fitting community amenity for a barangay health facility set among residential neighbors, encouraging family use of the site, per the source document.
scenario: The barangay health facility is surrounded by residential neighbors, bordered by a barangay chapel on one side and a municipal water pumping station on another.

q: Among these materials, which has the lowest embodied energy?
n: Wood requires comparatively little processing energy to produce, giving it the lowest embodied energy among the materials listed, per the source document.
scenario: The design team is choosing finish materials for the barangay health facility.

q: Which location best suits the parking area?
n: Placing parking on the south side keeps it close to the road frontage along the site's southwestern edge, allowing convenient vehicle access without cutting through the facility's interior.
scenario: The lot's road access runs along its southwestern edge, giving that side full southwestern exposure.

q: Per the zoning ordinance, how should this proposed facility be classified?
n: A national-government health facility falls under the General Institutional (GI) zoning category, which covers community-to-national-level institutional uses such as health and government service buildings, per PD 1096 IRR, Rule VII, Table VII.1 (Zoning Classification).
scenario: A national government agency is building a General Institutional (GI) barangay health facility.

q: Laying out gypsum board for maximum sheet efficiency over the 75-square-meter eave area, how many boards are required?
n: A standard gypsum board sheet measures 1.22 m x 2.44 m (about 2.98 sq. m.). Dividing the 75 sq. m. eave area by this sheet size gives about 25.2 sheets; rounding up for full-sheet coverage gives 26 pieces.
scenario: The facility's eaves total 75 square meters and are to be finished in gypsum board.

q: For an exterior paint finish, which color scheme works best?
n: White-and-gray tones read as clean, neutral, and institutional, reinforcing the facility's public-health character while keeping maintenance simple, per the source document.
scenario: This is a national-government-developed, General Institutional (GI) barangay health facility.

q: Which architectural style suits this project best?
o: Modern, with clean and textured lines
n: A modern approach with clean, textured lines suits the practical, contemporary image expected of a government health facility, per the source document.
scenario: The facility is a General Institutional (GI) barangay health project undertaken by the national government.

q: On which side of the site should the playground ideally sit?
n: Locating the playground on the east side, away from the road frontage to the southwest, keeps children's play areas removed from vehicular traffic and the site's public entry zone, and gives them gentler morning sun rather than the harsher afternoon sun.
scenario: The lot's road access runs along its southwestern edge, giving that side full southwestern exposure.

q: With a suspended ceiling above the waiting area, what finish should the concealed CHB masonry joints in the plenum space receive?
n: A “kostura” (rough scratch coat) finish is sufficient for masonry joints hidden within a concealed plenum, since they are never exposed to view and don't warrant a smooth finish coat, per the source document.
scenario: The waiting/congregation area is designed with a suspended ceiling above CHB masonry walls.

q: Which space should connect directly to the waiting/assembly area?
n: The reception area should be directly accessible from the waiting area so arriving patients can be received and directed without delay, per the source document.
scenario: The floor plan of the barangay health facility is organized around a central waiting/congregation area.

q: Which structural system is most recommended here?
n: A trabeated (post-and-beam) system is a straightforward, economical structural approach well-suited to a low-rise government health facility of this scale, per the source document.
scenario: This project is a low-rise, General Institutional (GI) barangay health facility.

q: Given the site's orientation, where should a utility building, if included, be placed?
n: Placing the utility building at the western corner keeps back-of-house/service functions away from the neighboring water pumping station to the southeast and screened from the public entry sequence, following the same layout logic as before with the site turned so the road runs along the southwestern edge.
scenario: The lot's road access runs along its southwestern edge, with a barangay chapel to the northwest and a municipal water pumping station to the southeast.

q: Which flooring material best suits the waiting/assembly area?
n: Vinyl tile flooring is durable, low-maintenance, and comfortable underfoot, which suits a high-traffic public waiting area in a health facility, per the source document.
scenario: This is the waiting/congregation area of the barangay health facility.

q: To maximize the facility's lighting, which distribution type is preferred?
n: Diffused lighting spreads illumination evenly across a space and reduces glare and harsh shadows, maximizing usable light coverage, per the source document.
scenario: The lighting scheme spans the facility's public and clinical spaces.

q: Per the occupancy classification table in Rule VII of the National Building Code, which division does this facility fall under?
n: Health centers and similar facilities serving non-ambulatory patients fall under Group D, Division D-2 of the Institutional (Government and Health Services) occupancy classification, per PD 1096 IRR, Rule VII, Table VII.1, Group D, Division D-2.
scenario: A national government agency is building a General Institutional (GI) barangay health facility.

q: Which design character best expresses the facility's intent?
n: As a government-run community health facility, the design should read as understated and utilitarian while still maintaining a formal, institutional bearing, rather than a decorative or overly relaxed character, per the source document.
scenario: A national government agency is building a General Institutional (GI) barangay health facility.

q: Per BP 344, what slope is most desirable for a PWD-accessible pedestrian ramp?
n: BP 344's accessibility standards set 1:12 as the maximum allowable slope for a PWD ramp, per BP 344, IRR (Accessibility Law) — Ramp Slope Requirement.
scenario: PWD-accessible pedestrian ramps must be provided at the barangay health facility.

q: Given the site's dimensions and slope, what is the total elevation difference across the grade?
n: With an 18-meter frontage on a 1,350 sq. m. lot, the site depth is 75 meters (1,350 ÷ 18). At a 3% grade, the elevation change across that depth is 75 x 0.03 = 2.25 meters.
scenario: The rectangular, 1,350-square-meter lot has an 18.00-meter frontage and an overall 3% grade sloping toward the adjacent road.

q: Consistent with the project's objectives, which wall partition system best divides the facility's spaces?
o: Painted gypsum board on light-gauge steel studs
n: A 4-inch CHB masonry wall is a lightweight, cost-effective, and durable partition standard, appropriate for interior divisions in a government health facility, per the source document.
scenario: Per the project objectives, the facility's floor plan is divided into several distinct spaces.

q: Which window type suits this project best?
n: Jalousie windows offer maximum, adjustable natural ventilation, well-suited to a tropical-climate public health facility, per the source document.
scenario: The facility is being constructed in a tropical climate.

q: With a G.I. sheet roofing system, which structural member supports the gutter?
n: The “senepa” is the roof framing member along the eaves that carries and supports the gutter in a G.I. roofing system, per the source document.
scenario: A G.I. sheet roofing system covers the facility's roof.

q: Which lighting color temperature suits the waiting area best?
n: Cool white CFL lighting produces brighter, more alert illumination appropriate for a clinical/public waiting space, per the source document.
scenario: This is the facility's waiting/congregation area.

q: Which column cross-section best minimizes torsion or moment in the structure?
n: A square column section resists bending equally in both directions, minimizing torsional or moment imbalance compared with a rectangular section, per the source document.
scenario: The facility is a low-rise, General Institutional (GI) barangay health project.

q: Which material best suits door knobs and handles?
n: Brass hardware is durable and has natural antimicrobial properties, making it well-suited to frequently-touched fixtures in a health facility, per the source document.
scenario: Door hardware is being specified across the facility.

q: Which interior wall finish best suits the waiting/assembly area?
n: A white semi-gloss paint finish is economical, easy to clean, and brightens the interior — practical for a public health facility, per the source document.
scenario: This is the barangay health facility's waiting/congregation area.
